note: Twenty-five pages, nineteen measured regions on fifteen of them, and the printed count closes: fifteen figures and three tables own a region each, and one algorithm box is refused. The arithmetic is exact for the exhibits and broken for the last content page - p24 is a zero-text full-page raster with no measured region - which is declared in the rule list rather than repaired. Three caption pairs share one printed line, so four captions are typed from the crop and a line-start-only detector finds twelve of the fifteen figure captions.
rules: Nineteen measured regions on fifteen of twenty-five pages resolve into fifteen figure rows, three table rows and one refusal, and the paper prints eighteen exhibit numbers - Figures 1 to 15 and Tables 1 to 3 - with no duplicate number, no number cited and never printed, and no printed number left without a caption. The census therefore closes on the printed count: eighteen numbers, eighteen rows. The one content page with no region is p24, the article sheet, and it is declared below rather than counted. [caption.numbering] is "Figure N:" on all fifteen figure rows and "Table N:" on all three table rows.

The caption detector needs a second pass on this paper: THREE pairs of figure captions print on one shared line - Figure 9 with Figure 10 on p19, Figure 12 with Figure 13 on p21, Figure 14 with Figure 15 on p22 - so a scan that only accepts a caption phrase that opens its line finds twelve of the fifteen figure captions and misses the second member of every pair. Two lines that look like bare caption heads are pointer tails, not captions: "Figure 3." on p7 and "Figure 6." on p12 are the wrapped ends of the sentences that name those figures. The twelve single-line captions are [caption.verbatim] as printed; the three second members of a pair are typed from the crop.

Caption side is class-fixed with no exception: all fifteen figure captions print BELOW the art, 15.1 to 15.3 pt under the region's bottom edge, and all three table captions print ABOVE the grid, 10.7 to 13.2 pt over the region's top edge. Both members of a side-by-side pair share one line and therefore one gap; [caption.position] records the split and no row departs from it.

Four captions are typed from the crop: each of Figures 12, 13, 14 and 15 is split across two printed lines and interleaved with its neighbour, so page 21 prints "Figure 12: Strategy score before      Figure 13: Strategy score after" over "optimization                          optimization" and page 22 prints "Figure 14: Change of Z under different Figure 15: Change of Z under different" over "n under m = 0.0233  m under n = 0.0021". The words are printed, the sentences are not, so no text-layer search matches them; the other eleven figure captions and all three table captions match their line exactly. [caption.words] counts the printed words of each, not the words of the two neighbours run together.

The three tables are live text and their dressing is one recipe: horizontal rules only, no vertical rule, no fill, no zebra row, on all three. Table 1 and Table 2 run all three rules to the full width. Table 3 splits its second rule into two short group rules - 253.6 pt under "Scores" and 104.8 pt under "Estimate", against 431.3 pt for the body rules - with an 11.7 pt gap between them, so its five horizontal segments are three printed rule lines and a rule that stops inside the table's own width. [table.rule_style] is booktabs on all three rows.

Units never ride in a header and mostly do not print at all: Table 1 spells them inside the definition prose, Table 2 prints four bare numbers under a caption that calls them conversion factors, Table 3 prints fifteen bare numbers with no unit on the header, the stub or a cell. [table.units_in_header] is false on all three rows.

Row counts are the printed counts, read off the text layer rather than off the rules: Table 1 prints one header and fourteen symbol rows, Table 2 one header and one data row, Table 3 two header rows and two data rows labelled Before and After. [table.rows] carries 15, 2 and 4 and [table.header_rows] carries 1, 1 and 2; Table 3 is the paper's only merged header, two spanning group labels over six column names.

Four exhibits open their page and belong to the section before it: Figure 5 prints at the top of p12 under the 3.5 heading from p10, Figure 6 at the top of p13 under 4.2.1 from p12, Figures 9 and 10 at p19 under 4.5 from p18, and Figure 11 at the top of p20 under 5.1 from p19. Figure 3 is the reverse: it prints at the top of p8 and belongs to 3.2.2 from p7, even though 3.2.3 opens the page it prints on. [place.section_path] follows the last heading above the region in document order, and every one of these rows would be filed one section late by a walk that restarts on the exhibit's page.

Twelve of the fifteen figures are named by number in the prose and three are never named: Figure 1 - which prints on p3 with no pointer anywhere - and Figures 14 and 15, the sensitivity pair on p22. Four pointers land on the page BEFORE their exhibit, so the lead is negative: Figure 5 is cited on p11 and prints on p12, Figure 6 on p12 and prints on p13, Figure 11 on p19 and prints on p20, Figure 12 on p20 and prints on p21. [mention.count] is zero on the three unnamed figures and [mention.lead_pages] is -1 on those four.

Families split sixteen ways from one vocabulary: map-or-plan-view 2, flowchart-or-schematic 2, other 3 (Figures 5, 6 and 7 are a pie, a donut and three donuts - no enum family names a share-of-total circle, so each carries an other_note), surface-or-3D 3, bar 2, line 2, composite-panel 1. [geometry.family] carries the split and [geometry.panel_count] the three multi-panel rows (Figures 2, 7 and 11). Every one of the fifteen figure regions holds exactly one embedded raster and not one drawing path - Figure 8's unit cube included - so no figure is drawn by the PDF here, while all three tables are live text.

The art contradicts the caption four times and the record keeps the printed caption: Figure 5 promises total carbon sequestration in billion tons and prints a 20-slice share-of-total pie with no unit, Figure 6 promises three-dimensional indicators and prints a flat donut with no value on any sector, Figures 14 and 15 promise the change of Z and their axes print carbon sequestration in million tons, and the p21 pair is captioned before and after while the two panels are drawn on different vertical scales (1.0 against 1.8). [caption.verbatim] carries what is printed in every case.

The last page of the body is a deficit: p24 carries no text layer at all and one raster covering the whole sheet (585.8 x 835.9 pt), the required newspaper article, and the layout pass measures NO region on it. It is content - the paper's one page of prose that the argument closes on - so it is declared here rather than recorded: the record cannot carry a bbox the measurement layer never produced, and p25 is the reference list. The same file's p10 algorithm box is the only region refused, filed not-an-exhibit. No row exists to carry p24, so no [caption.position] and no [caption.verbatim] is recorded for it, and the deficit sits in this rule list instead of in the counts.
